title: Looking and walking in 3D
description:
Write the maths of lesson 5.02's controller. Angles are in degrees:

```cpp
struct Vector3 { float x, y, z; };

Vector3 lookDirection(float yaw, float pitch);        // (cos p sin y, sin p, cos p cos y)
float clampPitch(float pitch);                        // -89 .. 89
float wrapYaw(float yaw);                             // into 0 <= yaw < 360
Vector3 wishDirection(float yaw, bool forward, bool back, bool left, bool right);
Vector3 orbitPosition(Vector3 target, float yaw, float pitch, float distance);
```

- `wishDirection` uses the **flat** forward `(sin y, 0, cos y)` and right `(-cos y, 0, sin y)`; forward and back add and subtract the forward direction, right and left the right direction; the sum is normalised (or `(0, 0, 0)`).
- `orbitPosition` is `target - lookDirection(yaw, pitch) * distance`: behind the target along the view.
hints: `fmod` keeps the sign of its first argument, so a negative yaw needs 360 added afterwards.
